title: Distance and size
about: Collocations for talking about distance (within walking distance, far-flung places, at close range) and size: when to say low, small, little or large, words like slim, plump and painfully thin, a great deal of, major and minor, and the difference between tall and high.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Українське «високий» англійською — tall або high. Tall — про людей і про те, що високе й вузьке: дерева, вежі, багатоповерхівки. High — про гори, стіни, стелі; про рівень чогось — ціни, відсоткові ставки, приплив; а також у сталих сполученнях high heels (високі підбори) і the high jump (стрибки у висоту). Записуй нові сполучення з tall і high, коли їх помічаєш.

items.phrase: a long / considerable / short distance from
items.pattern: be a long / considerable / short distance from sth · a short distance away · considerable is a bit formal
items.meaning: far from (long, considerable = quite a long way) or near to (short) a place
items.example: The campsite was a **considerable distance from** the nearest shop, so we took plenty of food with us.
more: Our flat is only a **short distance from** the park, which is great for walking the dog.
My grandparents' farm is a **long distance from** any town, so they do one big shop a month.
items.watchOut: «На великій відстані від» — a long / considerable distance from, без прийменника перед a: The school is a long distance from the station, не on a big distance. Big distance чути рідше, ніж long. У розмові найпростіше — a long way from: It's a long way from here.

items.pattern: be / live within walking / commuting / driving distance (of sth)
items.meaning: near enough to walk there, or to travel there and back for work every day
items.uk: у пішій доступності; так близько, що можна щодня їздити на роботу
items.example: We chose this flat because the shops and the station are all **within walking distance**.
more: My sister wants a job **within walking distance of** home so she can stop driving.
They moved to a village that's still **within commuting distance of** London.
items.watchOut: «У пішій доступності» — within walking distance (of sth). In walking distance теж іноді чути, але within — звичніше. Commuting distance — від commute: щодня їздити на роботу й назад. «Від чогось» тут зазвичай of: within walking distance of the station.

items.pattern: cover / travel 40 kilometres / 300 miles (a day) · cover a distance of… · cover the distance (between A and B)
items.meaning: go a particular distance on a journey
items.example: Our coach **covered** nearly 500 kilometres on the first day of the tour.
more: The ferry **covers the distance** between the two islands in forty minutes.
My uncle **travels** over 300 miles a week to visit his mum.
items.watchOut: «Подолати відстань» — cover a distance, не overcome a distance: overcome — подолати труднощі, страх. «Проїхати 40 кілометрів» — cover / travel / do 40 kilometres. Pass тут не підходить: pass a village — проїхати повз село.

items.pattern: far-off / far-flung places / countries / corners of the world · far-off lands
items.meaning: places that are very far away; far-flung often suggests far away and hard to reach
items.example: My aunt sends us postcards from **far-flung places** like Patagonia and Mongolia.
more: As a child, I read adventure books about **far-off** lands and dreamed of seeing them.
The charity sends nurses to **far-flung** villages that have no doctor.
items.watchOut: Пиши з дефісом: far-off, far-flung — це один прикметник перед іменником. Просто far places звучить незвично; кажуть far-off / faraway / distant places. Не плутай із far-fetched — «надуманий, малоймовірний» (a far-fetched excuse) і far-reaching — «далекосяжний» (far-reaching changes).

items.pattern: at close range · at such close range · from close range · see / photograph sth at close range
items.meaning: from very near
items.example: In the safari park we saw lions **at close range**, just a few metres from the car.
more: At the airport we saw our favourite footballer **at such close range** that we could have touched him!
Photos taken **at close range** show every detail of a butterfly's wings.
items.watchOut: «Зблизька» — at close range або close up, не at near distance. Range тут — відстань, з якої щось видно чи можна дістати. Close у цьому значенні — /kləʊs/ зі звуком «с»; дієслово close (закрити) — /kləʊz/.

items.pattern: a neighbouring town / village / country / area · in neighbouring towns
items.meaning: a town, country or area that is next to or near the one you are talking about
items.uk: сусіднє місто / сусідня країна / сусідній район
items.example: There's no swimming pool in our village, so we go to the one in the **neighbouring town**.
more: Lots of shoppers come over the border from **neighbouring countries** at the weekend.
The fire spread quickly to **neighbouring areas** of the forest.
items.watchOut: «Сусідній» перед іменником — neighbouring (американське написання — neighboring), а не neighbour town: neighbour — це людина, сусід. Про сусідню кімнату чи будинок частіше кажуть next door: the house next door.

items.pattern: low prices / wages / pay / levels (of sth) / interest rates · opposite: high
items.meaning: prices, pay or amounts that are below the usual level
items.example: People drive from all over the region to this market because of its **low prices**.
more: Many young nurses leave the job because of **low pay** and long hours.
Tests showed only **low levels** of pollution in the river this year.
items.watchOut: Ціни, зарплати й рівні бувають low і high, а не small і big: low prices, low wages, a low level of inflation. «Маленька зарплата» — найчастіше low pay / low wages (a small salary теж кажуть). Дешевими (cheap) зазвичай називають речі, а ціни — низькими (low).

items.pattern: small quantities / numbers / amounts (of sth) · in small numbers · a small number of people · a small amount of money
items.meaning: not much or not many of something
items.example: The farm shop only makes this cheese in **small quantities**, so it often sells out.
more: Only **small numbers** of tourists visit the island in winter.
Add the salt in **small amounts** and taste as you go.
items.watchOut: «Невелика кількість» — a small amount / number / quantity, зазвичай не a little amount. Little працює інакше, без amount: a little sugar, a little time. Amount — з незлічуваними (a small amount of money), number — зі злічуваними (a small number of people).

items.pattern: large quantities / numbers / amounts (of sth) · in large numbers · a large number of people · a large amount of money
items.meaning: a lot of something
items.example: Supermarkets throw away **large quantities** of food every day.
more: Swans come to the lake in **large numbers** every winter.
Don't carry **large amounts** of cash when you travel.
items.watchOut: З amount, number і quantity найприродніше звучить large: a large number of people, a large amount of money. Big тут теж чути в розмові, але large — звичніше. «Багато людей» — a large number of people, а не a large quantity of people: quantity — про речі й речовини.

items.pattern: a small / large increase (in sth) · also a small / large rise / fall / decrease
items.meaning: a rise that is not big / a rise that is big
items.example: There's been a **small increase** in the price of bread this month.
more: Our landlord asked for only a **small increase** in rent this year.
The town has seen a **large increase** in the number of people who cycle to work.
items.watchOut: «Невелике підвищення» — a small increase, не a little increase. «Значне» — a large / big increase. Прийменник — in: an increase in prices, in rent. Наголос: іменник — an INcrease, дієслово — to inCREASE.

items.pattern: on a large / small / smaller scale · a large-scale / small-scale project · a large-scale map (detailed, of a small area)
items.meaning: big / small in size or amount; a large-scale map shows a small area in a lot of detail
items.uk: у великих / малих масштабах; великомасштабна (детальна) карта
items.example: My parents grow vegetables **on a small scale**, just enough for the family.
more: The new factory will make furniture **on a large scale** for shops all over Europe.
The guide gave us a **large-scale map** of the island with every footpath on it.
items.watchOut: «У великих масштабах» — on a large scale, з on, не in. Large-scale map — карта великого масштабу, тобто детальна карта невеликої місцевості (1:25 000), а не карта всього світу.

items.pattern: adjective + little + noun: poor little Joe, a nice little room, a dear little dog · informal, friendly
items.meaning: little after another adjective makes the phrase sound warm and friendly; it is not only about size
items.example: **Poor little** Max fell off the swing and grazed his knee.
more: We found a **nice little** café round the corner from the hotel.
What a **sweet little** puppy! Can I stroke him?
items.watchOut: Little тут працює як українські пестливі суфікси: a nice little room — «гарненька кімнатка». Small так зазвичай не вживають: poor small boy звучить дивно. Порядок слів: спочатку оцінка, потім little — a lovely little house, не a little lovely house.

items.pattern: my little brother / sister (= younger) · opposite: big brother / sister · informal
items.meaning: a younger brother or sister
items.example: I have to take my **little sister** to school every morning.
more: My **big brother** taught me to ride a bike.
Even at forty, he's still my **little brother**, and I still worry about him.
items.watchOut: «Молодший брат» — little brother (розмовне) або younger brother, не small brother. «Старший» — big brother / older brother, у британській ще elder brother. Little brother може бути й дорослим: ідеться про вік, а не про розмір.

items.pattern: a little problem · (lots of) little things / jobs to do · = not very important
items.meaning: something small and not very important
items.example: There's just one **little problem**: I've forgotten my wallet.
more: I've got lots of **little things** to do before we go on holiday.
It's the **little things** that make a hotel feel special, like fresh flowers in the room.
items.watchOut: «Дрібниці, дрібні справи» — little things / little jobs. Small things теж кажуть, але коли йдеться про щось неважливе, little звучить природніше. Порівняй: a little problem — «невелика проблема», а a little time — «трохи часу».

items.pattern: make sb look / feel small · try to make sb look small (in front of others)
items.meaning: make someone seem stupid or unimportant, especially in front of other people
items.example: My boss criticised me in front of the whole team just to **make me look small**.
more: Good teachers never **make** a pupil **look small** for giving a wrong answer.
He loves telling stories that **make** his brother **look small** at family parties.
items.watchOut: «Принизити когось» — make sb look / feel small, без to: make me look small, не make me to look small. Little тут не вживають: не make sb look little.

items.pattern: make small talk (with sb) · be good / bad at small talk
items.meaning: talk politely about unimportant things, like the weather, with people you don't know well
items.uk: вести світську бесіду, розмовляти про всяке-різне
items.example: At the wedding I had to **make small talk** with relatives I'd never met.
more: I'm not very good at **small talk**, so big parties tire me out.
The hairdresser **made small talk** about the weather while she cut my hair.
items.watchOut: «Підтримувати розмову ні про що» — make small talk, не do / lead small talk і не little talk. Small talk незлічуване: без a і без -s.

items.pattern: a fat / slim book / volume / file · also fat / slim people
items.meaning: a thick book with lots of pages / a thin book with few pages
items.example: I took a **fat book** on holiday, and it lasted me the whole two weeks.
more: Her first book was a **slim** collection of short stories.
Our doctor pulled out a **fat** file full of my old test results.
items.watchOut: Fat і slim кажуть і про книжки, і про людей; про книжку ще кажуть thick / thin. А от plump чи skinny про книжку зазвичай не кажуть. Про людину fat звучить прямо й часто грубо; ввічливіше — overweight або a bit big.

items.pattern: a plump / skinny person / child / face / arms · about people (and animals), not books
items.meaning: plump: a little fat, in a soft, pleasant way; skinny: very thin, often in a way that doesn't look healthy
items.example: Grandma always says healthy babies are **plump** and pink.
more: He was a **skinny** teenager, but now he goes to the gym every day.
Our cat was **skinny** when we found her, but she's getting **plump** now.
items.watchOut: «Повний» про людину — не full: I'm full означає «я наївся». Кажуть plump (повненький, м'яко), overweight (ввічливо) або fat (прямо, часто грубо). Skinny — «худий, кощавий», часто з несхваленням; slim — «стрункий», це комплімент.

items.pattern: painfully thin · also painfully shy / slow
items.meaning: so thin that it upsets or worries you to look at them
items.example: After months in hospital, my grandad was **painfully thin**.
more: The stray dog was **painfully thin**, so we fed it every day.
She was **painfully shy** as a child and hid behind her mum.
items.watchOut: Painfully тут не означає, що комусь болить: «аж боляче дивитися», тобто дуже. Painfully thin кажуть про людину чи тварину, а не про книжку чи річ.

items.pattern: a great deal of + uncountable noun: time / money / energy / enthusiasm / help · not big / large
items.meaning: a lot of
items.example: Planning the wedding took **a great deal of** time and patience.
more: Our neighbour has **a great deal of** experience with gardens, so ask her.
The kids showed **a great deal of** enthusiasm for the school play.
items.watchOut: Тільки a great deal of (або a good deal of), не a big deal of і не a large deal of.

items.phrase: a major / minor change / difference / effect
items.pattern: a major / minor change / difference / effect (on sth) · make major changes · make a major difference (to sth)
items.meaning: a big and important / a small and not important change, difference or effect
items.example: Moving to the countryside made a **major difference** to our lives.
more: There have only been a few **minor changes** to the café since my grandparents went there.
The dry summer had a **major effect** on the harvest.
items.watchOut: Major — «значний, головний», а не «майор» і не «мажорний». Minor — «незначний, другорядний», а не «мінорний» (сумний). У розмові a big / small change теж природно; major / minor звучить трохи серйозніше.

items.phrase: a major / minor difficulty / issue / point / factor
items.pattern: a major / minor difficulty / issue / problem / point / factor (in sth)
items.meaning: an important / unimportant problem, question, part of an argument, or reason
items.uk: серйозна / незначна проблема, питання, аргумент, чинник
items.example: Cost was a **major factor** in our decision to go camping instead of staying in a hotel.
more: We had a few **minor difficulties** with the car, but nothing serious.
Parking is a **major issue** in the town centre.
items.watchOut: «Серйозна проблема» — a major / serious problem або issue, не a heavy problem і не a strong problem. Factor — чинник, причина, що впливає на рішення: a major factor in sth, з in.

items.pattern: a tall man / woman / tree / building / tower · 1.90 metres tall · taller than · the tallest
items.meaning: higher than usual; used for people and for things that are high and narrow
items.example: My son is only fourteen, but he's already **taller** than me.
more: There are some very **tall trees** in the park behind our house.
From the top of the **tallest building** in the city you can see the sea.
items.watchOut: Українське «високий» — tall або high. Про людей — тільки tall: a tall man, не a high man (he's high — «він під кайфом»). Про дерева, вежі й багатоповерхівки зазвичай кажуть tall; high building теж трапляється, але tall звичніше.

items.pattern: high mountains / hills · also a high wall / fence / ceiling · 3,000 metres high · the highest mountain
items.meaning: rising a long way above the ground
items.example: The village sits among **high mountains**, and the road is closed when it snows.
more: Our old flat had **high ceilings** and huge windows.
The garden is surrounded by a **high wall**, so nobody can see in.
items.watchOut: Гори — high: high mountains, the highest mountain in Europe (tall mountain теж іноді чути, але high звичніше). Висоту гори, стіни чи паркану кажуть через high: The wall is two metres high. High — про те, що сягає високо від землі, а не про зріст.

items.pattern: high prices / interest rates / rents / costs · prices are high · opposite: low
items.meaning: costing a lot of money
items.example: **High prices** in the city centre mean that many young people can't afford to live there.
more: We waited to buy a house because **interest rates** were so **high**.
Ski resorts often have very **high prices** in February.
items.watchOut: Ціни бувають high або low, не big і не tall. Дорогими (expensive) зазвичай називають речі й послуги: The shoes are expensive, але The prices are high. Interest rate — відсоткова ставка за кредитом чи вкладом.

items.pattern: (wear / walk in) high heels · high-heeled shoes · opposite: flat shoes
items.meaning: shoes, usually women's, with a heel that lifts the back of the foot well off the ground
items.example: My feet hurt after dancing all night in **high heels**.
more: She never wears **high heels** to work because she walks a lot.
My mum bought **high-heeled** boots for my brother's wedding.
items.watchOut: «На підборах» — найчастіше in high heels: walk / dance in high heels. Heels тут — самі туфлі на підборах. Tall heels кажуть рідко, стандартно — high heels. Heels /hiːlz/ з довгим «і» — не плутай із hills /hɪlz/ (пагорби).

items.pattern: (at) high tide · opposite: low tide · the tide comes in / goes out
items.meaning: the time when the sea reaches its highest level on the beach
items.example: At **high tide** the beach almost disappears, so we always go when the tide is out.
more: The sea comes right up to the café's windows at **high tide**.
Check the times of **high** and **low tide** before you walk across to the island.
items.watchOut: «Приплив / відплив» — high tide / low tide, або the tide comes in / goes out. Найчастіше з at і без артикля: at high tide. Не tall tide.

items.pattern: the high jump · do / win the high jump · compare: the long jump
items.meaning: a sport in which people jump over a bar that is raised higher and higher
items.example: My daughter came second in **the high jump** at the school sports day.
more: He set a new school record in **the high jump**.
My brother was good at **the high jump** but hopeless at running.
items.watchOut: «Стрибки у висоту» — the high jump, «у довжину» — the long jump: в однині й з the. Не the height jump і не jumps in height.

warmup.uk: Мій брат дуже високий, майже два метри.
warmup.q: My brother is very ___: almost two metres.
warmup.explain: Про людей кажуть tall. High — про гори, ціни, стіни, приплив.

warmup.uk: Мій молодший брат ще ходить у садочок.
warmup.q: My ___ brother still goes to nursery.
warmup.explain: Молодший брат — little brother (або younger brother), не small brother.

warmup.uk: Ремонт кухні коштував нам купу грошей.
warmup.q: Redoing the kitchen cost us a ___ deal of money.
warmup.explain: Багато — a great deal of (+ незлічуване). A big deal of і a large deal of не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Ціни на квартири в столиці дуже високі.
warmup.q: The prices of flats in the capital are very ___.
warmup.explain: Ціни бувають high або low. Tall — про людей, дерева, будинки.

warmup.uk: У нашому місті низький рівень безробіття.
warmup.q: Our town has a ___ level of unemployment.
warmup.explain: Рівень, ціни, зарплати — low або high, а не small чи little.

warmup.uk: Від готелю до моря можна дійти пішки.
warmup.q: The sea is within ___ distance of the hotel.
warmup.explain: У пішій доступності — within walking distance.

warmup.uk: Учора ми пройшли пішки п'ятнадцять кілометрів.
warmup.q: Yesterday we ___ fifteen kilometres on foot.
warmup.explain: Подолати відстань — cover. Overcome — подолати труднощі чи страх.

warmup.uk: У ліфті він завжди намагається завести розмову ні про що.
warmup.q: In the lift he always tries to make ___ talk.
warmup.explain: Розмова ні про що — small talk; make small talk — підтримувати таку розмову.

A.q: The castle is a ___ distance from the station, so take a taxi.
A.explain: Чимала відстань — a considerable / long distance. Wide і high з distance не вживають.

A.q: The doctor looked at the mole on my arm at ___ range with a magnifying glass.
My cousins live in the ___ village, just two kilometres away.
A.explain: Сусіднє село — the neighbouring village. Neighbour — людина, сусід; neighbourhood — район, околиця.

B.q: I'd like a ___ amount of rice, please, not a full plate.
B.explain: Невелика кількість — a small amount. Little з amount зазвичай не вживають, few — лише зі злічуваними в множині.

B.q: The ___ increase in the price of petrol has made everyone angry: it's up by a third.
B.explain: Значне підвищення — a large increase. Tall — про зріст, little increase не кажуть.

B.q: Our club does charity work, but only on a small ___.
B.explain: On a small / large scale — у малих / великих масштабах.

C.q: The puppy has got a bit ___ since we started giving it treats.
C.explain: Пухкенький — plump. Full — ситий, skinny — худий, кощавий.

C.q: My cousin came back from the expedition ___ thin: he'd lost fifteen kilos.
C.explain: Painfully thin — страшенно худий, аж боляче дивитися.

C.q: There's no ___ difference between the two flats: both have two bedrooms and a balcony.

M.q: Who's the ___ person in your family?
Borrowing money is expensive right now because interest rates are ___.
M.explain: Ставки й ціни бувають high або low. Expensive — про речі й послуги.

M.q: The ferry can only enter the harbour at ___ tide, when the water is deep enough.
M.explain: Приплив — high tide, відплив — low tide.

practice.q: The airport is a considerable ___ from the city, so allow an hour for the taxi.
The bakery is only a ___ distance from our flat, so I buy fresh bread every morning.
The new hospital is a long distance ___ the bus station, so most patients come by car.
We need a flat within ___ distance of my office, because I don't want to spend hours travelling every day.
Grandma likes her new flat because the doctor's is within ___ distance.
Shops, a park and a school are all ___ walking distance of the house.
Our old car has ___ over 200,000 kilometres, so it's time for a new one.
How far can you ___ in a day on an electric bike?
In the school fun run, children ___ a distance of two kilometres.
Our neighbour is a wildlife photographer who travels to ___ places, from the Arctic to the Amazon.
Grandpa told us stories about pirates and treasure on far-___ islands.
We'd love to visit ___ countries like Peru and Nepal one day.
The tennis players walked right past us, and we saw them at ___ range.
The fox didn't run away, so we could photograph it at very close ___.
Have you ever seen a tiger ___ close range?
When the bridge closed, drivers had to go through the ___ village to get to the motorway.
During the floods, people from ___ villages came to help with sandbags.
This supermarket chain is famous for its ___ prices, but the queues are long.
Many young people leave the village because of ___ wages and the lack of jobs.
Doctors were worried about the ___ level of vitamin D in her blood.
The bank is offering very ___ interest rates, so it's a good time to borrow.
The medicine is safe in ___ amounts, but don't take too much.
Only a ___ number of people came to the meeting, so it finished early.
This rare bird is now found only in small ___ along the coast.
The factory uses ___ quantities of water, so it was built next to the river.
Fans arrived in ___ numbers, and the stadium was full an hour before the match.
The new restaurant spent ___ amounts of money on advertising.
A large ___ of snow fell overnight, and the schools were closed.
There's been a ___ increase in bus fares: just ten pence.
The new park has led to a ___ increase in visitors: there are twice as many as last year.
Since the new road opened, there's been a large increase ___ traffic in our street.
The bakery started ___ a small scale, in the owner's kitchen.
The company now grows strawberries on a ___ scale and sells them to every supermarket in the country.
Our town has the same traffic problems as the capital, just on a ___ scale.

example.title: Our new old house
example.uk:
Минулої весни ми переїхали з міста й купили старий фермерський будинок. Він на чималій відстані від найближчого супермаркету, але звідти я все ще можу щодня їздити на роботу: долаю потягом близько 60 кілометрів на день.

Будинок потребував дуже багато роботи. На кухні ми зробили значні зміни, а нагорі — лише невеликі. Мій молодший брат приїхав допомогти, але витрачав години на дрібниці, як-от вибір дверних ручок.

Найкраще тут — краєвид: на півночі високі гори, а довкола саду — високі дерева. Минулого тижня в сад зайшов олень, і ми спостерігали за ним зблизька з кухонного вікна. До сусіднього містечка ми тепер майже не їздимо. Кому потрібні ті магазини?
example.en:
Last spring we left the city and bought an old farmhouse. It's a [[considerable distance from|a1]] the nearest supermarket, but my office is still [[within commuting distance|a2]]: I [[cover|a3]] about 60 kilometres a day by train.

The house needed [[a great deal of|c4]] work. We made [[major changes|c5]] to the kitchen and only small ones upstairs. My [[little brother|b7]] came to help, but he spent hours on [[little things|b8]], like choosing door handles.

The best part is the view: [[high mountains|m2]] to the north and [[tall trees|m1]] round the garden. Last week a deer walked into the garden, and we watched it [[at close range|a5]] from the kitchen window. We hardly ever go to the [[neighbouring town|a6]] now. Who needs shops?
